questions.question: The finance director of a building materials supplier is reviewing an AWS proposal just after the company negotiated a bulk discount on replacement servers for its own data center. She asks what AWS actually means by the value proposition of the AWS Cloud. Which statement captures it?

options.A: Computing spend becomes a fixed annual fee that stays flat no matter how much capacity the company consumes
options.B: Up-front purchases of owned capacity are replaced with on-demand resources that are started and stopped as demand requires
options.C: AWS takes over responsibility for operating and securing everything the company runs, including its applications and data
options.D: The strongest argument is that most large suppliers in the building trade have already moved their systems to the cloud

rationale.correct: The value proposition of the AWS Cloud is trading capital-heavy, slow-to-change owned infrastructure for on-demand capacity: the company provisions resources when demand appears and releases them when it fades, instead of buying hardware years ahead of need. The recent server discount does not change that structural argument.

distractors.A: This inverts the pricing model: AWS charges are usage-driven and variable, not a flat annual fee independent of consumption.
distractors.C: The shared responsibility model leaves the customer responsible for its applications, data, and configuration; AWS does not absorb everything the company runs.
distractors.D: What other suppliers have done is an observation about the market, not the value proposition; the argument rests on the cost-structure change, not on imitation.

questions.question: An adventure tour operator based in Auckland wants to start selling guided trips to customers in Chile, Norway, and Japan next quarter, with the booking system responding quickly in each market. The operations lead assumes this requires leasing server space in each country first. Which benefit of the AWS global infrastructure answers this concern?

options.A: Elasticity, which adjusts the capacity of the booking system up and down as seasonal demand changes
options.B: AWS Direct Connect, which provides a dedicated private network link from the Auckland office into AWS
options.C: A phased plan that delays each market launch until a local hosting contract has been signed in that country
options.D: Global reach with speed of deployment: infrastructure launches in AWS Regions near each market as a configuration step

rationale.correct: Presence in many geographies is itself the benefit: the AWS global infrastructure turns entering a new market into a configuration step. Global reach and speed of deployment mean the operator can run the booking system close to customers in each country without leasing anything locally.

distractors.A: Elasticity matches provisioned capacity to demand in both directions; it says nothing about where in the world that capacity runs.
distractors.B: AWS Direct Connect links a fixed site into AWS; it is a connectivity service for the office, not a mechanism for serving customers in new geographies.
distractors.C: Waiting for local hosting contracts recreates the slow path the global infrastructure exists to remove; the capacity is already deployed in Regions near each market.

questions.question: A campus shuttle service runs a bus-tracking backend that automatically grows to forty instances during term time and shrinks to four each summer, and riders have never noticed an outage. When the university asks which cloud benefit the automatic growing and shrinking demonstrates, what is the correct answer?

options.A: Elasticity: provisioned capacity follows demand in both directions, expanding for the term and contracting for the summer
options.B: Agility: the path from an idea to a running system is shorter than it would be in a traditional data center
options.C: AWS Auto Scaling: the service that adds instances to the fleet and removes them as load changes
options.D: High availability: a fleet that resizes itself is automatically protected against outages of any kind

rationale.correct: Matching provisioned capacity to demand in both directions is the definition of elasticity. The question asks for the cloud benefit being demonstrated, and elasticity is exactly the property the growing and shrinking fleet exhibits.

distractors.B: Agility describes shortening the path from idea to running system; the scenario describes capacity following demand, not delivery speed.
distractors.C: AWS Auto Scaling is the service that implements the behavior; the question asks for the property being demonstrated, and a service name is not a cloud benefit.
distractors.D: High availability keeps a service reachable through failure. Resizing a fleet with demand does not by itself protect against outages, and the absence of outages is a separate property from capacity matching demand.

questions.question: A chartered surveying practice has been running its mapping workloads on AWS for two years and wants structured design guidance to review them against AWS best practices. Which instrument provides the review lens?

options.A: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF), which organizes an enterprise's journey into the cloud
options.B: An AWS Support case asking a support engineer to review the architecture and report back with findings
options.C: The AWS Well-Architected Framework, the set of pillars and design principles for workloads already on the cloud
options.D: The AWS Well-Architected Tool, the console service that records and tracks workload reviews

rationale.correct: Design guidance for workloads already running on the cloud is the AWS Well-Architected Framework: its pillars and design principles are the review lens the practice applies to its own architecture.

distractors.A: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) governs the journey into the cloud - organizing an adoption effort, not reviewing workloads that already run there.
distractors.B: Handing the review to a support case defers the practice's own judgment; the published framework exists precisely so the team can apply the review lens itself.
distractors.D: The AWS Well-Architected Tool runs and records a review; the guidance itself - the lens the review applies - comes from the framework, not the tool.

questions.question: A city zoning department is preparing its permit-application workload for a first AWS Well-Architected review and wants the team to know the framework's actual pillars before the session. Which TWO of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Fault tolerance
options.B: Operational excellence
options.C: Increased revenue
options.D: Sustainability

rationale.correct: The six pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. Of the options offered, operational excellence and sustainability are the two genuine members of the set.

distractors.A: Fault tolerance sounds like a plausible member, but it is not a pillar; designing for failure lives inside the reliability pillar.
distractors.C: Increased revenue is one of the business outcomes AWS associates with the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, not a Well-Architected pillar.
distractors.E: Elasticity is a benefit of the AWS Cloud - capacity matching demand - not one of the six pillars of the framework.

questions.question: During a Well-Architected review at a beverage bottling plant, the discussion turns to the line-telemetry workload: it must keep operating through the loss of an Availability Zone and recover quickly from any disruption. The plant manager keeps steering the conversation back to the size of the monthly bill. Under which pillar does the recover-from-disruption concern belong?

options.A: Cost optimization, the pillar the plant manager's concern about the monthly bill falls under
options.B: Reliability, the pillar that owns a workload's ability to recover from disruption and continue operating
options.C: Performance efficiency, the pillar about matching resources to the demands of the workload
options.D: High availability, the pillar dedicated to keeping services reachable through component failure

rationale.correct: Recovering from disruption is the reliability pillar's territory: identifying differences between the pillars means placing a stated design concern under the pillar that owns it, and continuing to operate through the loss of an Availability Zone is a reliability concern.

distractors.A: The bill is a real concern, but it is a different concern; assigning the recovery question to cost optimization answers the loudest voice in the room instead of the stated design issue.
distractors.C: Performance efficiency owns matching resources to demand; the concern described is disruption recovery, which belongs to a different pillar.
distractors.D: High availability is a cloud benefit, not a Well-Architected pillar; the pillar that owns recovery from disruption is reliability.

questions.question: The board of an agricultural seed distributor has approved a move to AWS and assumes this means shutting the data center and moving every system in a single weekend cutover. What should the IT director explain about how organizations adopt the cloud?

options.A: Adoption follows a chosen strategy: the organization selects among cloud adoption strategies and sequences workloads deliberately
options.B: A single undifferentiated cutover is correct, since running cloud and data-center systems side by side only adds confusion
options.C: Adoption should be postponed until every system has been rewritten for the cloud, and then completed in one final step
options.D: Every system must be moved unchanged first in all cases, because that is the universally recommended migration practice

rationale.correct: Cloud adoption is a planned strategy rather than a single lift event: an organization chooses among cloud adoption strategies and sequences workloads deliberately, which is exactly what the board's weekend-cutover picture misses.

distractors.B: Collapsing the move into one undifferentiated cutover removes the sequencing an adoption effort needs; mixed environments during a transition are normal, not a defect.
distractors.C: Waiting for every system to be rewritten postpones value indefinitely and converts a manageable sequence into one large, riskier event.
distractors.D: Moving everything unchanged is one available strategy, not a universal rule; applying it in all cases ignores the choice the organization is supposed to make.

questions.question: A coffee equipment importer wants a data-driven business case - an inventory of its current servers, their utilization, and a projected AWS run cost - before the board will approve a migration, and it has no budget yet for outside help. Which resource supplies this?

options.A: AWS Pricing Calculator, which estimates the monthly cost of a planned AWS architecture
options.B: A paid engagement with a consulting firm to produce a bespoke migration assessment
options.C: AWS Migration Hub, which tracks the progress of migrations that are already underway
options.D: Migration Evaluator, which analyzes the current environment and builds a projected business case

rationale.correct: Among the resources that support the cloud migration journey, Migration Evaluator is the one that starts from the existing environment - inventory and utilization - and produces a data-driven business case, before any paid engagement is bought.

distractors.A: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates a design you specify going forward; it does not analyze the importer's current environment or produce a business case from it.
distractors.B: A paid assessment buys machinery the problem does not yet warrant; a no-cost resource that produces exactly this business case already exists.
distractors.C: AWS Migration Hub tracks migrations in progress; the importer needs the analysis that comes before a migration starts.

questions.question: An actuarial consulting firm at the start of its cloud journey adopts the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) to organize the effort, and the partners ask what business outcomes AWS associates with it. Which TWO are among them? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Reduced business risk
options.B: Performance efficiency
options.C: Increased revenue
options.D: A flat monthly AWS bill that does not vary with usage
options.E: Transfer of the customer's security responsibilities to AWS

rationale.correct: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) is the instrument that organizes an adoption effort, and four business outcomes are attached to it: reduced business risk; improved environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance; increased revenue; and increased operational efficiency.

distractors.B: Performance efficiency is a pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, a different instrument; it is not one of the AWS CAF business outcomes.
distractors.D: AWS pricing remains usage-driven; a flat bill is not how cloud charges work and is not an outcome the framework promises.
distractors.E: The shared responsibility model still applies after adoption; the customer keeps its side, and the AWS CAF does not transfer it.

questions.question: An apartment listings portal must move its listings database to AWS while agents keep writing to it around the clock; the cutover window is minutes, not hours. The database administrator proposes keeping the on-premises database and a cloud copy synchronized until the moment of switchover. Which migration approach is this?

options.A: Deferring the database move until the rest of the estate has migrated and accepting a stale copy meanwhile
options.B: A one-time bulk export restored into the cloud database during a scheduled overnight outage window
options.C: Database replication, keeping the on-premises source and the cloud copy synchronized until the moment of cutover
options.D: Rebuilding the listings data in a different database engine as part of the move to avoid carrying the old schema

rationale.correct: Keeping the source and the cloud copy synchronized until switchover is database replication - the classic approach for moving a data tier with minimal disruption. It fits a system that takes writes around the clock and a cutover window measured in minutes.

distractors.A: Deferral leaves the hardest move for later while its cost compounds; the scenario asks to identify the approach proposed, and postponement is not it.
distractors.B: A bulk export needs an outage window and misses writes that land after the export; the stem rules out exactly that downtime.
distractors.D: Changing the database engine mid-move adds a redesign the problem does not require; the task is moving the data tier with minimal disruption, not re-architecting it.

keywords: cost savings of moving to the cloud
questions.question: The CFO of a cold-chain trucking fleet budgets a large hardware purchase every few years plus fixed data-center contracts, and asks what structurally changes about costs if the telematics platform moves to AWS. Which answer describes the change?

options.A: Up-front capital spending on owned capacity becomes usage-driven, variable operating spend that tracks actual consumption
options.B: Variable operating costs are converted into fixed capital costs, making the annual budget easier to predict
options.C: Total cost is guaranteed to fall for every workload the fleet moves, whatever its usage pattern
options.D: Logistics firms that moved report large savings, so the same percentage can be booked into next year's budget without analysis

rationale.correct: The cost-structure change funds every other cloud economic argument: up-front, capital, fixed spending on owned capacity becomes usage-driven, variable operating spend. Fixed costs give way to variable costs that track consumption, which is where the cost savings of moving to the cloud actually originate.

distractors.B: This states the change backwards: cloud spending moves away from fixed capital outlays toward variable, usage-driven operating costs, not the other way around.
distractors.C: Cloud economics changes the cost structure; it does not guarantee a lower total for every workload regardless of usage pattern.
distractors.D: Other firms' outcomes are anecdotes about different workloads; the structural change is what the analysis should highlight, and savings still have to be assessed, not booked on imitation.

keywords: costs that are associated with on-premises environments
questions.question: An art print marketplace is comparing the full cost of its co-located server room with a proposed AWS deployment. Which TWO cost line items would disappear from its budget entirely once the workloads run on AWS? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Rack space, power, and cooling charges for the server room
options.B: Spending on compute capacity for the storefront during business hours
options.C: License fees for the commercial database engine the storefront uses
options.D: Periodic hardware refresh purchases as servers reach end of life
options.E: Operating system patching effort, which AWS performs for every service after migration

rationale.correct: Facility costs - space, power, cooling - and the hardware refresh cycle are costs that are associated with on-premises environments and have no cloud equivalent: AWS owns the buildings and the servers. Comparisons that omit them understate what the server room really costs.

distractors.B: Compute spending does not disappear; it changes shape, from owned capacity to usage-driven charges for what the storefront consumes.
distractors.C: A commercial license can travel with the workload under a Bring Your Own License model or be replaced by an included license; either way the line item does not simply vanish.
distractors.E: Patching duty depends on the service: on Amazon EC2 the guest operating system remains the customer's to patch, so the effort does not disappear for every service.

questions.question: An athletic footwear brand owns perpetual licenses for a commercial database engine and intends to keep using those entitlements when the database moves onto AWS compute. Which licensing model describes this arrangement?

options.A: A conversion model in which the one-time license purchase becomes a flat monthly software fee charged by AWS
options.B: An AWS Marketplace subscription that replaces the perpetual licenses with software procured through the catalog
options.C: License-included pricing, in which the cost of the software license is bundled into the hourly rate of the service
options.D: The Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model, in which the entitlements the brand already owns travel with the workload

rationale.correct: Using licenses the organization already owns on cloud infrastructure is the Bring Your Own License [BYOL] model: the entitlement travels with the workload instead of arriving with the service. The alternative - included licenses - would mean paying for the license as part of the service rate.

distractors.A: No such conversion happens; a perpetual license the brand owns stays owned, and AWS does not restate it as a flat monthly software fee.
distractors.B: AWS Marketplace is a procurement channel for acquiring new software; the brand is reusing entitlements it already holds, not buying replacements.
distractors.C: License-included pricing describes the opposite arrangement: the license arrives with the service and is paid for in its rate, not carried in by the customer.

questions.question: A car wash franchise runs its booking system on instances sized three years ago; average utilization now sits below ten percent even at peak. Finance wants the monthly bill reduced without changing how the application works. What is the appropriate first action?

options.A: Rewrite the booking system as event-driven serverless functions so idle capacity disappears altogether
options.B: Rightsize the instances: match the provisioned resource size to the demand that is actually observed
options.C: Purchase Reserved Instances for the existing instances to obtain a discount on the current shape
options.D: Set a billing alarm on the account so finance is alerted whenever monthly spend rises any further

rationale.correct: Rightsizing is the deliberate cost action that matches provisioned resource size to observed demand. Utilization evidence is already in hand, the application does not need to change, and resizing the oversized instances is the direct, reversible first step.

distractors.A: A serverless rewrite redesigns the workload, which the franchise explicitly did not ask for; rightsizing is distinct from re-architecting.
distractors.C: A Reserved Instance discount on an oversized shape locks in the oversizing; buying a discount is distinct from correcting the size.
distractors.D: A billing alarm watches spend after the fact; the cause - oversized instances - is already known and can be acted on directly.

questions.question: Across an animal shelter network, staff create a test copy of the adoption system by hand each week and often forget to delete it, leaving idle environments running for weeks. The operations lead asks what automating the provisioning and teardown would actually change. What is the answer?

options.A: Little would change; the better fix is one larger shared test environment with enough capacity for every team
options.B: It would mainly improve reporting, with a quarterly audit catching any environments left running too long
options.C: It removes both the staff time spent on manual setup and the spend on forgotten idle environments
options.D: The same result comes from a checklist that makes each staff member responsible for remembering the deletion step

rationale.correct: The benefits of automation are a cost lever as well as a speed lever: automated provisioning and teardown remove the weekly manual toil and stop the meter on environments nobody remembered to delete. The saving shows up in staff time and in the monthly bill at the same time.

distractors.A: A larger shared environment adds capacity where the problem is process; the waste comes from environments outliving their use, not from having too little room.
distractors.B: A quarterly audit discovers idle environments long after they started costing money; automation prevents the idle time instead of reporting on it.
distractors.D: A checklist pushes the failure onto the people who already forget; automating the teardown removes the reliance on memory altogether.

questions.question: The CFO of a board-game publisher notices that an hour of compute on AWS costs less than the equivalent hour on the publisher's own rack servers, even before staffing is counted, and asks what makes that price possible. Which explanation is correct?

options.A: The publisher's own usage volume has reached the level at which AWS grants automatic volume discounts
options.B: Shifting spending from capital purchases to operating expense is what lowers the price of each compute hour
options.C: The lower price comes from Reserved Instance discounts that AWS applies to all customers by default
options.D: Economies of scale: AWS aggregates demand from a large customer base, and its lower unit costs show up in pricing

rationale.correct: Economies of scale are the mechanism: a provider aggregating enormous demand achieves lower unit costs - hardware, power, operations - than any single customer can, and those unit costs surface in the published price. The publisher's own volume or commitments are separate, additional levers.

distractors.A: This attributes the price to the customer's own volume; the mechanism in question is the provider's aggregate scale, which benefits every customer at any size.
distractors.B: The capital-to-operating shift changes the structure of the publisher's spending; it does not by itself make a compute hour cheaper to deliver.
distractors.C: Reserved Instance discounts are a commitment the customer chooses, not a default applied to everyone; the baseline price is already lower for a different reason.

questions.question: An ambulance dispatch service is briefing new engineers who have never worked with a cloud provider, and its head of platform wants them to be able to state plainly what the AWS shared responsibility model divides. Which description states what the model divides?

options.A: It splits duties between the AWS Regions a workload runs in and the Availability Zones inside those Regions
options.B: It assigns every security duty to AWS, which operates the infrastructure and everything a customer places on it
options.C: It splits security duties into security of the cloud, which AWS operates, and security in the cloud, which the customer owns
options.D: It ranks security duties by severity, giving the customer the highest-risk items and AWS the remainder

rationale.correct: The AWS shared responsibility model answers one question: who secures what. Recognizing the components means naming both halves - security of the cloud, the infrastructure AWS operates, and security in the cloud, the data, configuration and access decisions the customer owns. Every AWS service inherits that division.

distractors.A: Regions and Availability Zones describe where a workload runs, not who secures it; the model's division is unrelated to that geography.
distractors.B: Handing every duty to AWS collapses the model into one side; the customer keeps its data, its access decisions, and the configuration of what it runs.
distractors.D: Severity ranking is a risk-management activity the customer performs afterwards; it is not the line the model draws.

keywords: describing the customer's responsibilities on AWS
questions.question: An aquaculture farming group runs its harvest-tracking application on Amazon EC2 instances that were launched from a standard Linux image. During an insurance audit the group's IT lead is asked which security duties belong to the group itself. Which TWO of the following are the customer's responsibilities? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Classifying the harvest records the application stores and deciding who may open them
options.B: Maintaining the physical security of the facilities that house the instance hardware
options.C: Configuring the virtualization layer that isolates one customer's instances from another's
options.D: Applying operating system patches to the guest instances the group has launched
options.E: Signing the audit report that certifies the underlying infrastructure as compliant

rationale.correct: Describing the customer's responsibilities on AWS means naming the duties the customer can actually reach: data classification and access decisions, and guest configuration such as patching the operating system on instances it launched. Describing AWS responsibilities covers the rest - facilities, hardware, and the virtualization layer beneath the instance.

distractors.B: Physical security of the facilities is squarely security of the cloud; the group has no access to those buildings and no duty over them.
distractors.C: The virtualization layer sits below the customer boundary, so this is a real control the group cannot configure at all.
distractors.E: AWS Artifact supplies audit reports and attestations to the customer; the customer does not certify AWS's infrastructure.

keywords: responsibilities that the customer and AWS share
questions.question: A community college district's auditor insists that every control in the security plan name exactly one owner. The district's cloud lead objects, pointing to patch management, where AWS patches the platform beneath the workload and the district patches its own guest instances. What does the shared responsibility model say about controls of this kind?

options.A: They are shared controls: AWS and the customer each carry the control at a different layer
options.B: They belong to AWS, whose patching of the underlying platform also covers the guest instances
options.C: They should be recorded as exceptions and disclosed to the auditor as controls without an owner
options.D: They are inherited controls, which the customer takes over in full on the day it adopts the platform

rationale.correct: Patch management is the model's third category - responsibilities that the customer and AWS share. AWS patches the infrastructure and its managed-service internals; the district patches the guest instances it runs. One control name, two owners, each at a different layer, is a valid entry in a security plan.

distractors.B: AWS patching stops at the boundary of what it operates; a guest instance the district launched stays the district's to patch.
distractors.C: Recording the control as an unowned exception documents the confusion instead of resolving it, and both owners are in fact identifiable.
distractors.D: Inherited controls are those the customer gains without action, such as data center access control; patch management is not handed over in full.

questions.question: A concrete supply company runs its scheduling database on Amazon EC2 and is about to move it to Amazon RDS. Its security committee wants the standing task apply database engine patches to stay with the company's own operations team after the move. What changes about that task?

options.A: Nothing changes: engine patching stays with the company on every AWS service it runs
options.B: The company keeps the task and now performs it from the AWS Management Console instead
options.C: The task disappears altogether, and no party patches the engine once the data has moved
options.D: AWS takes over engine patching, and the company is left with data, access, and configuration

rationale.correct: The responsibility boundary moves with the service model. On Amazon EC2 the company owns the guest operating system and the database engine installed on it. On Amazon RDS, as on AWS Lambda, AWS operates those internals, and what remains for the company is its data, its access decisions, and the service configuration.

distractors.A: Treating the boundary as fixed is the error the move exposes: the same duty sits on different sides depending on the service.
distractors.B: Changing where a task is performed is a surface change; the question is which party performs it, and after the move it is not the company.
distractors.C: The engine is still patched - by AWS, on its own schedule; a managed service does not leave the software unmaintained.

questions.question: A conference organizing bureau has just closed the server cupboard where a locked door and a visitor sign-in sheet were its only physical controls. Its operations manager, who expects little to change, asks what the bureau actually gains on the security side by running on AWS. Which answer is correct?

options.A: Its applications become immune to stolen credentials once they run on AWS infrastructure
options.B: It inherits the physical and infrastructure controls AWS operates, and gets encryption as configuration
options.C: It transfers the whole security program to AWS, including its applications and its stored data
options.D: It replaces its own security controls with the products it buys through AWS Marketplace

rationale.correct: The benefits of cloud security begin with inheritance: the bureau gets the physical and infrastructure controls AWS already operates, audited at a scale a server cupboard cannot reach. On top of that, capabilities that were projects in a small office - encryption of stored data and of traffic, centralized logging - become configuration choices.

distractors.A: No platform makes an application immune to stolen credentials; identity and access management stays a customer duty on AWS.
distractors.C: Security in the cloud does not transfer: the bureau still owns its applications, its data, and who may reach them.
distractors.D: AWS Marketplace is a procurement channel for additional products; the inherited platform controls arrive with the service itself.

questions.question: A cooking school network's payment processor requires that the keys protecting stored card data sit in dedicated cryptographic hardware the network itself controls, in a module holding a recognized validation. The network already terminates every connection with TLS. Which control does that requirement call for?

options.A: TLS on every connection already meets it, as the card data is protected all the way to storage
options.B: A managed key service, in which AWS creates and holds the keys on shared infrastructure
options.C: AWS CloudHSM, dedicated cryptographic hardware the network controls for protecting stored data
options.D: Nothing further, as AWS encrypts everything written to its storage as a platform property

rationale.correct: The two states are distinct. TLS delivers encryption in transit, which protects data while it moves; the processor's requirement is about encryption at rest, and specifically about who controls the module holding the keys. Dedicated, validated cryptographic hardware under the network's own control is what a mandate of that kind names.

distractors.A: Protecting the journey is a real control at the wrong point: once the card data lands, transit protection no longer applies to it.
distractors.B: A managed key service is the usual answer for key management, but it does not give the network its own validated hardware module.
distractors.D: Storage encryption is a customer configuration on AWS, not an automatic property, and it would still not satisfy a dedicated-hardware mandate.

keywords: auditing with AWS CloudTrail and AWS Config
questions.question: A corporate travel desk discovers that a security group was widened overnight and must establish which identity made the change, from which address, and at what time. Its dashboards already carry CPU and network graphs for every instance. Which service holds that record?

options.A: Amazon CloudWatch, whose metric graphs already cover activity across the account
options.B: AWS Config, which reports the security group's configuration against the desk's rules
options.C: The operating system logs on the instances, which record administrative actions on the host
options.D: AWS CloudTrail, whose event history names the API call and the identity that made it

rationale.correct: Auditing with AWS CloudTrail and AWS Config answers two different governance questions. CloudTrail keeps the account-wide event history of API activity - which identity called what, when, and from where - which is exactly the record a change investigation needs. Monitoring with Amazon CloudWatch covers metrics and logs about how resources are performing, which is where the CPU and network graphs come from.

distractors.A: Metrics describe how resources behave, not who acted on them; no CPU or network graph names the caller behind a change.
distractors.B: AWS Config audits resource configuration and its history, so it shows that the rule was broken, not which identity broke it.
distractors.C: Host logs are a real record at the wrong layer: the security group was changed through the AWS API, never on the instance.

questions.question: A courthouse records office must give its external auditor a current copy of an AWS compliance report before the audit window closes at the end of the week. The office has no support plan beyond basic account access. Where does it obtain that report?

options.A: AWS Config, after enabling the rule set that matches the auditor's control framework
options.B: AWS Artifact, which provides AWS audit reports and attestations for download on demand
options.C: AWS Support, by opening a case that asks for the current report to be sent to the office
options.D: AWS Security Hub, whose posture scores stand in for the compliance report the auditor wants

rationale.correct: AWS Artifact is the self-service source of AWS audit reports and attestations: the office signs in, accepts the terms, and downloads the current document itself. That is a different job from monitoring, configuration auditing, or threat detection, none of which produce a third-party attestation.

distractors.A: AWS Config evaluates the office's own resources against rules; it does not publish AWS's audit reports.
distractors.C: Routing the request to a support case adds a wait that the self-service source removes, and the deadline is days away.
distractors.D: A posture score describes the office's own configuration; an auditor asking for an AWS attestation will not accept it.

keywords: compliance requirements that vary among AWS services
compliance needs among geographic locations or industries
questions.question: A crane hire company working across three countries has confirmed that AWS holds the compliance certification its safety regulator names. Its project manager concludes that every AWS service the company adopts is therefore covered by that certification. What is wrong with the conclusion?

options.A: A service's presence in a compliance program varies by service, so coverage is checked per service
options.B: Nothing is wrong; a certification held by AWS extends to every service offered in the account
options.C: The obligation belongs to AWS, so confirming coverage for each service is AWS's task and not the company's
options.D: The gap is closed by buying a compliance product for each service through AWS Marketplace

rationale.correct: Compliance obligations are not uniform. They differ by geography and by industry, which is why compliance needs among geographic locations or industries have to be established first, and there are compliance requirements that vary among AWS services, so a program that covers one service does not automatically cover the next. Checking the specific service against the program's scope is part of selecting it.

distractors.B: Certification is granted for named services in named scopes; treating it as an account-wide property is the misreading the audit will find.
distractors.C: AWS publishes which services are in scope for which program, but choosing services that satisfy the regulator remains the company's decision.
distractors.D: AWS Marketplace sells software; it does not add a service to the scope of a compliance program.

questions.question: A crop insurance agency has been warned by its legal team that claim documents carrying policyholder identifiers may have been uploaded over the past year into a general-purpose Amazon S3 bucket. The agency needs to find out which stored objects actually contain those identifiers. Which service does that job?

options.A: Amazon Inspector, whose assessments cover software vulnerabilities and network exposure
options.B: Amazon GuardDuty, whose threat detection flags the uploads as suspicious data movement
options.C: Amazon Macie, which discovers and classifies sensitive data held in Amazon S3
options.D: Server-side encryption on the bucket, which removes the need to identify the objects

rationale.correct: Each detection service answers a different question. Discovery and classification of sensitive data already sitting in Amazon S3 is Amazon Macie's job: it inspects the objects and reports which of them carry identifiers of the kind the legal team named.

distractors.A: Amazon Inspector assesses software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure; it does not read the contents of stored objects.
distractors.B: Amazon GuardDuty detects threat activity such as unusual API calls, so an ordinary upload by an authorized user raises nothing.
distractors.D: Encryption protects the objects but answers no part of the question the agency asked, which is which documents hold identifiers.

questions.question: A cruise line reservations team is setting up AWS Identity and Access Management [IAM] for a dozen new analysts who all need the same permissions and who will work across two AWS Regions. Which TWO statements about IAM are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Permissions attach to an individual IAM user only, so each analyst needs a policy written for them
options.B: Groups collect users, so one permission set can serve every analyst on the team at once
options.C: IAM users are Regional, so each analyst needs a separate user in each Region they work in
options.D: One shared sign-in for the analysts is acceptable while their permissions are identical
options.E: AWS managed policies can be attached as they are, with custom policies covering the rest

rationale.correct: AWS Identity and Access Management [IAM] gives each building block its own role: users carry long-lived identity, groups aggregate users so a single permission set serves many, and managed policies or custom policies carry the permissions themselves. IAM identities are global constructs, so the same user works in every Region.

distractors.A: Writing one policy per analyst removes the structure groups exist to provide and multiplies the maintenance for no gain.
distractors.C: IAM is global, not Regional; duplicating users per Region would be maintenance work that the service does not require.
distractors.D: A shared sign-in destroys attribution and widens exposure: any action taken traces back to the team rather than to a person.

questions.question: A dance studio chain hands a contractor full administrator permissions for a two-week booking-system migration, on the reasoning that a short engagement is low risk and that scoping the access down would slow the work. Which principle does the arrangement violate?

options.A: Multi-factor authentication, which the contractor should have been enrolled in first
options.B: The principle of least privilege, which grants only the permissions a task requires
options.C: Delegated administration, under which an administrator approves each action taken
options.D: Root user protection, which forbids sharing account credentials outside the chain

rationale.correct: The principle of least privilege sizes every permission set to the task in hand: the contractor needs the permissions the migration requires and nothing beyond them. Duration does not change the principle - a short engagement with administrator permissions is still an oversized grant, and the studio can scope it without slowing the work.

distractors.A: A second authentication factor proves who is signing in; it says nothing about how much the signed-in identity may do.
distractors.C: Approving each individual action is heavier than the situation warrants and still leaves the oversized permission set in place.
distractors.D: Root user protection is a real obligation at a different layer: what was granted here is an administrator permission set, not the root account.

keywords: importance of protecting the AWS root user account
questions.question: At a debt collection agency the finance director signs in as the account root user every morning to look at the bill, and a long-lived root access key sits in the nightly billing script. Which TWO measures protect the root user? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Attach a read-only IAM policy to the root user so the morning check can change nothing
options.B: Rotate the root access key each quarter and write the new value into the billing script
options.C: Enable multi-factor authentication [MFA] on the root user and keep the device secured
options.D: Share the root credentials with a second director so that no one person holds them
options.E: Delete the root access key and give the finance director an IAM identity for daily work

rationale.correct: The importance of protecting the AWS root user account comes from what it can do: it is the one identity whose permissions cannot be reduced. The measures that hold are a strong unique password with multi-factor authentication [MFA] enabled, no standing access keys at all, and everyday work moved to an IAM identity so the root user is reached only for the tasks that genuinely require it.

distractors.A: The root user's authority does not come from an attached policy, so attaching a restrictive one does not limit what it can do.
distractors.B: Rotation shortens the life of each key while leaving a standing root credential in a script, which is the exposure worth removing.
distractors.D: Splitting knowledge of the credentials across two people widens who can act as root and blurs which of them did.

keywords: tasks that only the account root user can perform
questions.question: A diamond certification lab has moved all of its daily work onto IAM identities and now asks whether the root user can be retired entirely, since nobody has needed it for months. Which task still requires the account root user?

options.A: Closing the AWS account and changing the registered account name and email address
options.B: Creating IAM users and attaching the managed policies each laboratory team needs
options.C: Viewing the account's bills and downloading the monthly invoices for the finance team
options.D: Deleting an Amazon S3 bucket that holds the lab's archived certification records

rationale.correct: The tasks that only the account root user can perform are a short list of account-level operations - closing the account, changing the registered account name, email address, or payment details, and a handful of similar changes to the account itself. That list is why the root user stays reachable, protected, and otherwise unused.

distractors.B: Identity administration is exactly what an IAM administrator does, which is why the lab has managed without the root user for months.
distractors.C: Access to billing information can be delegated to IAM identities once the account activates it, so it is not a root-only task.
distractors.D: Deleting a bucket is a resource action governed by permissions; any identity with those permissions can perform it.

questions.question: A document shredding service runs a nightly reconciliation job on Amazon EC2 that reads a database password and a third-party courier token. Both values sit in the job's source file, which is committed to the team's repository. Where do those two secrets belong?

options.A: In environment variables set on the instance at launch, so the source file no longer holds them
options.B: In an encrypted copy of the source file, with the decryption password held by the team lead
options.C: In the access keys of an IAM user, rotated on the schedule the security policy names
options.D: In AWS Secrets Manager, which stores them and returns them to the job at run time

rationale.correct: Credential storage follows the access path. Access keys serve programmatic calls, passwords governed by a password policy serve console sign-in, and key pairs serve operating system access to an instance. Application secrets such as a database password or a courier token belong in AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager, which hand them to the job at run time and keep them out of source code.

distractors.A: The same plaintext secret is simply moved to another place on the same host, where it is still readable and still unmanaged.
distractors.B: Encrypting the file is a real control placed where it cannot help: the decryption password now has to live somewhere too.
distractors.C: Access keys authenticate a caller to AWS; they are not a store for a database password or a third-party token.

questions.question: An e-sports league operator keeps its tournament platform in one AWS account and its analytics workload in another. The analytics application, running on Amazon EC2, authenticates to the tournament account with an access key pasted into its configuration file. Which capability replaces that arrangement?

options.A: AWS IAM Identity Center, giving the analytics team single sign-on across both accounts
options.B: Multi-factor authentication on the analytics account, adding a second factor to the key
options.C: An IAM role in the tournament account that the analytics application assumes when it runs
options.D: A second copy of the access key, held in the tournament account for the application to use

rationale.correct: A workload that needs access in another account should assume a role there instead of holding a static key: cross-account IAM roles issue temporary credentials that expire on their own and can be scoped to exactly what the analytics workload reads. Nothing is pasted into a configuration file, so there is no long-lived secret to leak or rotate.

distractors.A: AWS IAM Identity Center is the answer for workforce sign-in, and this caller is an application rather than a person at a console.
distractors.B: A second factor applies to interactive sign-in; an unattended application cannot present one, so the pasted key would remain.
distractors.D: Copying the key into the other account multiplies the places a long-lived credential exists without shortening its life.

questions.question: An electrical contracting firm already keeps every employee record in its corporate directory and refuses to maintain a second set of AWS sign-in credentials for the same people. Its identity lead asks what federating the existing directory with AWS actually changes. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Each employee record is copied into IAM, which becomes the firm's system of record
options.B: Employees sign in against the corporate directory, which stays where the identity lives
options.C: The firm has to replace its corporate directory with an AWS-hosted one before sign-in works
options.D: Federating removes the need to define AWS permissions for the employees who sign in

rationale.correct: Among the types of identity management available, the federated option leaves the identity where it already lives: employees authenticate against the firm's own corporate directory, and AWS trusts the result. What changes is where sign-in happens, not who owns the employee record - which is exactly the second credential set the firm wanted to avoid.

distractors.A: Copying records into IAM is the opposite of federating and recreates the duplicate identity store the firm objected to.
distractors.C: Replacing a working directory is a large project the firm does not need; federation is built to reuse the directory in place.
distractors.D: Authentication and authorization stay separate: the firm still decides what a federated employee may do inside AWS.

questions.question: An escrow services company's public settlement portal has been hit twice this month: once by a traffic flood that saturated the front end, and once by injection strings submitted through its claim form. Which TWO services address these two threats? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Amazon Inspector, which assesses the portal's software for known vulnerabilities
options.B: AWS Firewall Manager, which administers protection policies across the company's accounts
options.C: AWS Shield, which defends the portal against distributed denial of service floods
options.D: AWS WAF, which inspects web requests and blocks malicious ones such as injection strings
options.E: AWS CloudTrail, whose event history shows the requests once the attack has ended

rationale.correct: The security capabilities that AWS provides map onto threats one by one. A volumetric flood against a public endpoint is what AWS Shield is built to absorb, and malicious web requests carried in form fields are what AWS WAF inspects and blocks at the request layer. Two different threats, two different protective services.

distractors.A: Amazon Inspector assesses software for known vulnerabilities; it does not stand in the traffic path and blocks nothing.
distractors.B: AWS Firewall Manager administers protection policies across accounts, so it needs those protections to exist before it can help.
distractors.E: An event history is a detective record produced after the fact, which is of no use while the portal is being saturated.

questions.question: An exhibition stand builder has one part-time security engineer who wants a standing source of AWS's own written analysis of new security features and practices, as reading material rather than an answer to a specific question. Which destination fits that need?

options.A: The AWS Knowledge Center, which answers the questions AWS customers ask most often
options.B: The AWS Security Center, the landing page gathering bulletins and compliance material
options.C: A case raised in AWS Support Center, answered in writing by an AWS support engineer
options.D: The AWS Security Blog, where AWS publishes its analysis of security features and practices

rationale.correct: Among the security-related documentation that AWS provides, each destination answers a different need. Ongoing analysis of new features and practices, written by AWS and published as reading material, is what the blog carries - which is what a single engineer keeping current actually wants.

distractors.A: The AWS Knowledge Center is organized around frequently asked questions, so it answers a question already formed rather than supplying reading.
distractors.B: The AWS Security Center gathers bulletins and compliance material, which is reference rather than the running commentary described.
distractors.C: Opening a case routes a specific problem to a support engineer, and no case is open here; it also puts a wait in front of public material.

questions.question: An eyewear retail chain has standardized on an intrusion-prevention appliance from an independent vendor and wants it running in front of its AWS workloads. Its procurement team is at capacity and will not open a new vendor onboarding process this quarter. How does the chain obtain the product?

options.A: Through AWS Marketplace, which lists third-party security products for purchase in the account
options.B: Through AWS Artifact, where vendor software is downloaded with its compliance documents
options.C: Through AWS Support, by asking the account team to arrange a license with the vendor
options.D: By dropping the appliance and using the nearest native AWS service in its place

rationale.correct: Third-party security products are procured through AWS Marketplace: the vendor's software is subscribed to inside the account and billed with AWS usage, which extends protection beyond the native services without opening a separate procurement channel. That is precisely the constraint the chain's procurement team imposed.

distractors.B: AWS Artifact supplies AWS's own audit reports and attestations; no vendor software is distributed through it.
distractors.C: Asking support to broker a license hands the task to someone else and still ends in a procurement process.
distractors.D: Abandoning a standardized appliance answers the procurement constraint by giving up the requirement it was meant to serve.

questions.question: A farm equipment dealership wants a recurring list of its own account hygiene problems - buckets left open to the public, IAM users without multi-factor authentication - rather than alerts about attacks under way. Which service produces that list?

options.A: Amazon GuardDuty, whose findings identify threat activity as it occurs in the account
options.B: AWS Config, which stores the configuration history of each recorded resource
options.C: AWS Trusted Advisor, whose security checks recommend fixes for the account's exposures
options.D: Amazon CloudWatch alarms on account metrics, raised whenever a threshold is crossed

rationale.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects an account and returns recommendations, and its security checks are aimed at exactly the hygiene issues named: public access where it was not intended, identities without multi-factor authentication, and similar standing exposures. It reports on the account's configuration, not on attacks in progress.

distractors.A: Amazon GuardDuty detects active threats, which is the opposite of what the dealership asked for.
distractors.B: AWS Config records how resources are configured and how that changed; turning that history into recommendations is a separate job.
distractors.D: A metric alarm fires once a threshold is crossed, so it reports symptoms after the fact instead of listing standing exposures.
